newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Reef Casino loses capital facility.
newsitem.headline: Reef Casino loses capital facility.

text.p: Casinos Austria International Ltd, operator of the Reef Casino, said on Thursday it had been advised by the Reef Casino Trust that financiers had withdrawn an external working capital facility.
The facility allows the casino to operate its junket/premium policy to attract high-stakes gamblers, mainly from Asia, chief executive officer Alexander Tucek told Reuters.

Casinos Austria said its junket/premium policy was now under review. However, together with trust manager Reef Casino Services, it was negotiating alternative agreements in order to avoid any interruption to high-stakes play.
Casinos Austria said the change affected an October agreement under which it agreed to prepay A$6 million in rent under its casino lease in two instalments.
Casinos Austria was now not obliged to pay the second instalment of A$3 million due on January 2, 1997, it said.

Reef Casino Trust announced in October it had made a A$5.9 million loss in the September quarter, saying the opening of its casino in the north Queensland tourist centre of Cairns had coincided with a disappointing period for tourism.
The Trust later announced it had hired merchant bank Grant Samuel and Associates to advise on a new capital structure for the trust as well as equity raising opportunities.
